# back-references and groups — `features/`

## Project layout

    features/
    ├─ checkout/ ❗                        the checkout feature (instance of
    │                                      [feature]/)
    │
    └─ [feature]/ 0+
       │
       ├─ steps/                           the feature's database steps
       │  │
       │  ├─ [step=0000]_{feature}.[kind={up,down}].sql 0+
       │  │  a step of this feature ({feature} repeats what [feature] matched)
       │  │
       │  └─ [step=0000]_[name=a+].sql 0+  a step of another table
       │
       ├─ {feature}.ts ❗                  the feature entry point (instance of
       │                                   [name=a+].ts, {feature} repeats what
       │                                   [feature] matched)
       │
       └─ [name=a+].ts 0+                  a module

❗ marks a named file or directory that must exist; one without it may be absent. A count after a pattern, such as `0+` or `1+`, is the fewest matching names that must exist.

In `[step=0000]`, the text after `=` is a mask: each character matches one character of the name. `0` matches a digit and `a` a lowercase letter. `+` repeats the element before it one or more times. `[kind={up,down}]` accepts exactly the listed names. `espalier help matching` has the full grammar.

## `[feature]/`
